judgments.title: MOHD NOR BIN ABD HAMID v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Criminal Law — Dangerous Drugs — Possession — Appeal against conviction and sentence — Charges under s 6(1) and s 12(2) Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 ("DDA") punishable under ss 39A(1) and 12(3) DDA — Drugs recovered from a sling bag — Whether possession (custody and control) established — Presumption of knowledge under s 37(d) DDA. Criminal Procedure — Appeal — Approach of appellate court to findings of fact of trial court — Appellate court must be slow to disturb findings of fact where trial court had the advantage of seeing and hearing witnesses — Herchun Singh v PP [1969] 1 MLRA 382 followed — But duty in a criminal appeal is to determine whether the conviction is safe, not merely whether the decision is wrong — Mohd Johi bin Said v PP [2005] 5 MLJ 409 applied. Criminal Procedure — Grounds of Judgment — Misdirection of fact — Trial Magistrate finding that drugs were recovered from accused's "right hand" when prosecution evidence was that drugs were recovered from a sling bag worn on the accused's body — Material contradiction between two conflicting scenarios in the same judgment — Prejudice to accused — Error not a mere typographical slip or lapsus calami — Section 422 CPC inapplicable — Tamilarasen Mohan v PP [2026] 1 MLRA 924 followed; Zulkefly bin Hadli v PP [2014] 6 CLJ 64 applied; Iyanar Thevar Gopalakrishnan v PP [1978] MLRAU 188 distinguished. Evidence — Possession — Chain of evidence — "Acu pakai" photograph — Investigating Officer admitting that the accused did not wear the sling bag on arrival at the police station, the bag having been carried separately — Photograph taken at the police station on the IO's own instructions — Chain of physical possession at the locus broken and contaminated — Custody and control not proved — Leow Nghee Lim v Regina [1956] 22 MLJ 28 considered; PP v Norhazwan Abd Wahab [2014] 4 MLJ 544 applied. Evidence — Adverse inference — Section 114(g) Evidence Act 1950 — Failure to investigate or produce CCTV footage of the locus — Bank premises with active CCTV — Best evidence withheld — Inference drawn against the prosecution — Saeid Reza Mohammadi Mohammad v PP [2016] 1 LNS 303 distinguished. Evidence — Section 8 Evidence Act 1950 — Flight as evidence of guilty mind — Absence of corroboration — No photographs of damaged road divider — No medical evidence of injury or damage to motorcycle — Prosecution's narrative of attempted escape unsupported and fragile. Evidence — Defence — Accused's explanation need only raise a reasonable doubt — Mohamad Radhi bin Yaakob v PP [1991] 3 MLJ 169 applied — Accused's explanation supported by IO's admission regarding the staged photograph — Reasonable doubt raised. Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 — Section 39A(1) — Sentence — 30 months' imprisonment and 4 strokes of whipping — Quantity of methamphetamine (18.30g) approaching threshold of s 39A(2) — Sentence reasonable and not excessive — Other sentences (12 months' each, concurrent) likewise reasonable. Words and Phrases — "possession" — "custody and control" — "staged reconstruction" — "miscarriage of justice".
judgments.judge: YA Tuan Avinder Singh Gill a/l Ranjit Singh

judgments.title: JAYSAKTHI A/L MANIMARAN v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Criminal Law — Dangerous Drugs — Possession — Section 6 Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 punishable under section 39A(2) — Cannabis 76.07 grams — Sole occupant and driver of vehicle — Drugs recovered at "bahagian handbrake" — Whether custody, control and knowledge proved beyond reasonable doubt — Ghasem Hozouri Hassan v PP [2018] 6 CLJ 133 applied. Criminal Procedure — Appeal — Appeal against conviction and sentence to High Court — Approach of appellate court — Court sitting in appellate capacity slow to disturb findings of fact of trial court — Conviction not to be disturbed if safe — Mohd Johi bin Said v PP [2005] 5 MLJ 409 and Herchun Singh v PP [1969] 2 MLJ 209 applied — Lai Kim Hon v PP [1981] 1 MLJ 84 followed. Criminal Procedure — Appeal — Power of appellate court — Section 316(b) Criminal Procedure Code — Power to reverse finding and sentence, affirm, enhance, reduce or order retrial. Evidence — Adverse Inference — Section 114(g) Evidence Act 1950 — Prosecution's failure to call witness who handed vehicle keys to accused — Whether material to genuinely live issue — Inference not drawn as a matter of course — Failure an omission in grounds of judgment but not a miscarriage of justice. Evidence — Possession — Physical improbability of location of drugs — Car owner's evidence that handbrake compartment "memang kecil" and package of 76.07 grams would not fit — Whether "bahagian handbrake" and "di depan handbrake" a material discrepancy or linguistic inarticulation — Contemporaneous Senarai Geledah and police report corroborating location — Not a material unreconciled discrepancy. Evidence — Investigation — Failure of investigating officer to investigate defence version — Whether drugs found at roadside or later at police headquarters — Defence version self-contradictory in cautioned statement, cross-examination and re-examination — Failure to raise reasonable doubt — Mat v PP [1963] 1 MLJ 263 considered. Evidence — Cautioned Statement — Section 37B(1) Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 — Specific and self-contained admissibility regime — Attachment of full unredacted cautioned statement as "Lampiran A" to prosecution's submissions impermissible — Whether trial court's finding tainted by inadmissible material — Finding read in context as based on admissible evidence — No miscarriage of justice. Criminal Law — Sentencing — Section 39A(2) Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 — Cannabis 76.07 grams — 11 years' imprisonment and 10 strokes — Whether manifestly excessive — Grading of sentence according to quantity relative to statutory threshold — Surentheran a/l Selvaraja v PP [2005] 2 CLJ 264 applied — Sentence reduced to 8 years' imprisonment; 10 strokes affirmed as statutory minimum.

judgments.catchwords: Criminal Law — Theft by clerk or servant — Penal Code s 381 — Common intention — s 34 — Warehouse assistant placing pallets of cartons on floor at supervisor’s instance — Trial court’s finding that accused acted ‘tanpa mengetahui apa tujuan’ — Absence of prior meeting of minds and pre-concerted plan — Non-compliance with WMS scanning procedure and FEFO policy equally consistent with innocence as with guilt — Accused absent at dinner when goods removed — Inference of shared criminal purpose unsustainable — Conviction unsafe — Appeal allowed; judgments.title: CHUNG CHEE YANG v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Criminal appeals - against the whole of the decision of the Magistrate’s Court Amendment of charges - s. 158(1) of the CPC grants the court broad discretion to alter or add to a charge at any point during a trial prior to the delivery of judgment - the optimal window to amend or introduce a charge is at the conclusion of the prosecution's case, provided that such an amendment does not cause irremediable prejudice to the substantive rights of the accused person Recall of witnesses following the amendment of a charge - the court's obligation to grant an opportunity to recall or re-summon past witnesses is triggered only upon a party's request, rather than operating as an automatic consequence of the amended charge - the trial court was under no legal duty to advise him of his rights under s. 162 of the CPC - the court is not under a duty to advise or prompt an accused person who is already fully and professionally represented by legal counsel on tactical choices or the exercise of procedural rights Presiding Magistrate recorded the guilty plea of the co-accused, before proceeding with the Appellant's trial - a presiding judge who records a co-accused's plea of guilt is not disqualified from continuing to try a remaining accused who has claimed his right to a full trial Criminal intimidation - essential ingredients of the offence comprise two prongs: first, the communication of a threat of injury to the victim's person, reputation, or property; and second, a distinct intent to cause alarm to that person - a threat need not be communicated through words alone; it may be manifested by conduct or any other threatening means - the omission of these verbal threats in the charge does not negate their existence or criminal intimidation The Prosecution’s failure to call the chief bodyguard - a settled principle that the Prosecution is under no legal obligation to call every available witness to narrate the same chain of events, provided there is no suppression or withholding of evidence Intention to shoot - a well-entrenched principle of criminal law that intention, being a subjective state of mind, may be proved through irresistible inferences drawn from the surrounding circumstances and is rarely capable of direct proof First information report - the primary purpose of a police report is to set the machinery of criminal investigation into motion. It is not required to contain every exhaustive fact. Instead, it suffices if the report enables the police to initiate an investigation. Defence as an afterthought - in criminal jurisprudence, the defence must present its case at the earliest possible stage. A failure to cross-examine on a core line of defence entitles the trial court to characterize it as a fabricated afterthought Custodial sentences - a sentencing court must be guided by the "one transaction rule" and the "totality principle".
